items.title: collect_mcycle_root_hashes returns at every automatic yield and rehashes the shadow state on each return and re-entry, so a yield loop makes every mcycle of a claim cost as much as a sampled one (~6000x at large periods)
items.component: src/machine.cpp machine::collect_mcycle_root_hashes / update_hash_tree; src/collect-mcycle-hashes-state-access.hpp do_write_mcycle
items.role: Honest operator (AUDIT.md row 1: collect_mcycle_root_hashes, hash tree)
items.severity: High (preferred) / Out of scope (if the outputs-or-yields exclusion excuses any bounded per-yield cost)
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: the yields exclusion applies only 'as long as ... each yield costs it a bounded amount (R12)'; step 1 says the application entries never excuse 'an emulator defect that its guest triggers'. Same split as R1-R8-3, so give both. 2 Role: honest operator. 3 High: 'lets the guest ... multiply the worst-case cost of an operation listed in R12 by a constant factor, compared with the same operation without the defect ... When the sizing is unknown, rate such a constant-factor increase High' -- operation 'a part of a claim'; no hash is required at a non-sampling automatic yield, yet each yield costs two shadow-page hash-tree updates (~20 us vs ~0.3 us in run()). 4 n/a. Distinct from R1-R8-3: that one is the write-TLB re-scan on entry and used these ~17 always-dirty pages as its control; fixing it leaves this cost.
items.reason: Variant of R1-R8-3 with a different site and fix: unconditional m_ht.update after every interpret return (machine.cpp ~2520) plus update_hash_tree's mark_always_dirty_pages on re-entry, and do_write_mcycle marking all shadow pages dirty. Code claims checked. High under sizing-unknown constant-factor case; OOS under literal yields exclusion.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: machine::collect_mcycle_root_hashes (src/machine.cpp) returns on every break other than reached_target_mcycle, including yielded_automatically. Inside its loop it calls m_ht.update(m_ars) after every interpret return whether or not the reached mcycle is a sampling point or fixed point (around line 2520), and on the next call's entry it calls update_hash_tree() (line ~2451), which runs mark_write_tlb_dirty_pages() and m_ars.mark_always_dirty_pages() (machine.cpp 1645-1649) before m_ht.update. collect-mcycle-hashes-state-access.hpp do_write_mcycle (lines ~147-157) also marks every page of AR_SHADOW_STATE_LENGTH dirty on every interpreter exit. So each automatic yield costs two hash-tree updates over at least the ~17 always-dirty shadow pages (the baseline that R1-R8-3's test used as its control), although the computation hash needs no hash at a non-sampling yield. This is distinct from confirmed R1-R8-3 (write-TLB re-scan on entry): with R1-R8-3 fixed, this cost remains. Trigger: a guest (taken over by an input) looping on 'sd t1,0(tohost); j .' with t1 = an automatic yield (e.g. progress, or tx-output length 0); the honest builder (prt.lua run_to_stop -> mcycle_computation_hash_run) re-enters after every yield. Required behavior: section 8 High, 'A defect that lets the guest ... multiply the worst-case cost of an operation listed in R12 by a constant factor, compared with the same operation without the defect ... A cost that the specified semantics require is not a defect. When the sizing is unknown, rate such a constant-factor increase High'; R12 lists 'a part of a claim'. Alternative reading: Out of scope under 'An application that tries to exhaust the honest operator through the number of its outputs or yields ... as long as ... each yield costs it a bounded amount (R12)'. Hunter evidence: scratch blind10/PERGUEST/cost.lua with guests g/spin.S and g/ayield.S: log2 period 10: spin 27.9 ns/mcycle, ayield via collect 20144 ns/mcycle (99999 calls), ayield via run() 147.6 ns/mcycle; log2 period 30: spin 3.2 ns, ayield 19485 ns; period 0 (every mcycle sampled) spin 18235 ns, i.e. a yield costs about a sample. rh.lua: collect call executing nothing ~10 us. Test idea (deterministic, no timing; model on bugs/R1-R8-3/test.lua which uses get_hash_tree_stats): with a 1-slot write TLB (so R1-R8-3 does not contribute), run K calls of collect_mcycle_root_hashes(MCYCLE_MAX, large log2 period, 0, 0) over an automatic-yield loop that writes no memory, and assert that hash-tree pages visited/hashes computed per yield-return are O(1) small (e.g. <= 2 pages, the pages actually written: htif tohost/fromhost and mcycle) rather than ~2x17 always-dirty shadow pages; compare against a control span with the same mcycles and no yields. Exit 1 on audit/prt2.

items.title: config.json size and unknown fields are unbounded, parsed in full on every load, and copied verbatim into every player snapshot by clone_stored
items.component: src/machine-config.cpp machine_config::load (read whole file + nlohmann parse, unknown keys ignored); src/machine.cpp machine::clone_stored (copies config.json verbatim)
items.role: Honest operator (AUDIT.md row 1: loading and cloning machines); PRT player (Support) propagates via clone_stored
items.severity: Critical (on-path adoption crash from unhashed data, as R1-O1-2) / High (template is data the operator may decline) / Low (cost linear in bytes supplied; R12 met)
items.rating_steps: 1 OOS: not the foreign-snapshot exclusion (hashed contents meet every valid-template condition); section 8: 'Once a snapshot meets them, nothing it carries outside the hashed state may ... crash the honest operator'; readings item 1 (loud refusal on adoption rated at step 4). 2 Role: loading/cloning = honest operator. 3 High: 'unbounded allocation in a component in the honest-operator role, caused by data from other parties that the honest operator may decline' if the template is declinable. 4 Critical: R12 'storing, loading, cloning ... bounded and at most linear in ... the bytes it covers' and R4 on 'Obtaining its valid template' if a compressible padded config (e.g. GBs of '[0,0,...]', ~8x parse amplification) OOMs adoption. 5 Low if load cost linear in the file's bytes is read as R12-conformant and one load+store normalizes it.
items.reason: Distinct from R1-O1-2 (different unhashed field, different fix: reject unknown members/bound config size, normalize on clone). Unsure: cost is linear in supplied bytes (Low reading) but unhashed, compressible padding can crash adoption (Critical/High readings). Keep.
items.brief_for_prover: Defect: machine_config::load (src/machine-config.cpp ~125-151) reads the entire config.json with os::read_file and parses it with nlohmann::json; unknown members (top level, in config, in ram) are silently ignored (ju_get_field); nothing bounds the file size. config.json is outside the hashed state and outside every valid-template condition. machine::store rewrites it normalized, but machine::clone_stored (src/machine.cpp ~566-570) copies it byte for byte, so the PRT player (prt.lua new_stored_player / commit / revert clones) propagates padding into every snapshot it creates and reloads. Trigger: a template supplier pads config.json of a valid template with an unknown member (e.g. a huge array of small integers, which compresses to almost nothing for transfer); the honest operator adopts it per O1 with cartesi.machine(T,{clear_hash_tree=true}) or the CLI --load --clear-hash-tree, or the PRT player. Required behavior: section 8 OOS entry 'Once a snapshot meets them, nothing it carries outside the hashed state may affect any transition (R1), crash the honest operator, or corrupt its memory'; R12 'storing, loading, cloning or syncing a machine' has 'a worst case in host time and memory that is bounded and at most linear in ... the bytes it covers'; R4 / 'Obtaining its valid template' on the honest operator's path (readings item 1: a valid template refused loudly on that path is rated at step 4). Compare confirmed R1-O1-2 (phtc_size) for the analogous unhashed-config precedent. Hunter evidence: a 60 MB unknown member: load still succeeds with the same root, peak RSS 458 MB vs 140 MB, CPU 1.66 s vs 0.37 s (scratch blind10/PERTEMPLATE/scripts). Test idea: copy bugs/harness/work/configs/baremetal-template/machine, add an unknown member to config.json (size chosen so that the parse amplification exceeds a ulimit -v/RSS allowance that the unpadded template plus a margin fits, e.g. allowance = control RSS + 2x the hashed state size), load with {clear_hash_tree=true} in a child process under that limit and assert it succeeds with root == root-hash.txt; and assert that clone_stored of the template produces a config.json no larger than machine:store would write (normalized). Fails today. Prover: also measure whether parse memory is >> file size (amplification) since that decides Critical/High vs Low.

threat_model_gaps: Guest software and decoded field meaning (R10-PERAPPDEV-3): section 3's guest-software Critical clause speaks of deviating 'from the rollup interface' and R7 of rx-buffer 'contents'; it does not say whether a guest tool that delivers a decoded input field in a unit its own linked API document contradicts (while the manual agrees with the tool) counts as a deviation, nor which document governs a guest tool's 'documented' use when the manual and the tool's package docs disagree.

Per-yield baseline (R10-PERGUEST-2, extends the R1-R8-3/R1-R14-1/R2-DFYIELD-1 gap): the High constant-factor case compares with 'the same operation without the defect', but when one confirmed defect's control (R1-R8-3: the ~17 always-dirty pages per yield) is itself avoidable work, the model does not say whether that baseline is 'a cost that the specified semantics require'.

Unhashed config bytes and R12 (R10-PERTEMPLATE-4): R12 bounds loading by 'the bytes it covers'; it is unclear whether unhashed, ignored config.json bytes count as bytes the load covers (then linear cost is conformant) or as data outside the hashed state that 'may not crash the honest operator' regardless of size, and whether parse-time memory amplification of such data is a constant-factor or an unbounded-allocation case.

Developer-time guest-tool defects (R10-PERAPPDEV-5 part c): a guest tool that, used as its API document says, makes template creation end at a non-accepted yield has no class other than Low; the model does not say whether guest-software scope covers defects that only invalidate the template rather than being triggered by an input.
